normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从围住羊群的低篱笆开始，再走到短短的发言与狭小的牢房。

normal.en: Con- is together and fine comes from finis, a border, so confine is to put a border around.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，fine 来自 finis（边界），所以 confine 就是在四周划出边界。

normal.en: A fence confines sheep just as a rule confines a discussion.
normal.cn: 篱笆圈住羊群，正如规则圈住讨论。

normal.en: To be confined to bed is to have a room the size of a mattress.
normal.cn: 卧床不起，就是把活动范围缩到一张床那么大。

normal.en: Confine and define both carry finis, the word for a boundary.
normal.cn: confine 与 define 都带着 finis，也就是边界这个词。

normal.en: A confined space feels small because the walls are doing their job.
normal.cn: 封闭空间显得小，是因为墙在履行它们的职责。

abstract.en: Picture a chalk line drawn around a pair of shoes.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈粉笔线画在一双鞋周围。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp lighting only one page.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯只照亮一页纸。

abstract.en: Picture a bird with a short string on its leg.
abstract.cn: 想象一只腿上系着短绳的鸟。

examples.en: Try to confine your answer to one page.
examples.cn: 尽量把答案限制在一页之内。

examples.en: She was confined to bed with a fever.
examples.cn: 她因发烧而卧床不起。

examples.en: The animals are confined in a small yard.
examples.cn: 这些动物被关在一个小院子里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 confine 记成 con（一起）加 fine（边界）：四面都划上边界，就是限制；被边界关住，就是禁闭。

root: 源自拉丁语 confinare（com 一起 + finis 边界），本义是共有一条边界，后引申为限制范围与禁闭。

sensesIntro.en: From sharing a border, to drawing a border around a topic, and finally to shutting a body behind walls.
sensesIntro.cn: 从共有一条边界，到给话题划出边界，最后到把身体关进墙内。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a low fence draws a circle, and everything must stay inside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈低篱笆划出范围，里面的东西都不能出去。

branches.en: Limiting a subject keeps a discussion from wandering.
branches.cn: 限制话题，能防止讨论四处游走。

branches.en: Confining a person or animal removes the choice to leave.
branches.cn: 把人或动物关起来，就是拿走了离开的选择。

branches.en: Both senses draw a line that cannot be crossed.
branches.cn: 两个义项都划出一条不能越过的线。

branches.en: A confined answer is often a clearer one.
branches.cn: 被限制范围的回答，往往更清楚。

branches.en: A confined space is small by design, not by accident.
branches.cn: 封闭空间的小是设计出来的，不是偶然。

intro.en: Confine is built on Latin com-, together, plus finis, a boundary.
intro.cn: confine 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 finis（边界）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin border base fin- also appears in define, final and finish.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的边界词基 fin- 也出现在 define、final 与 finish 中。

items.example: Confine the notes to one page.
items.exampleCN: 把笔记限制在一页之内。

items.example: The rule confines visitors to the hall.
items.exampleCN: 这条规定把访客限制在大厅内。

items.meaning: kept inside a place or limit
items.example: They confined the fire to one room.
items.exampleCN: 他们把火势控制在一个房间内。

items.example: The job felt confining to him.
items.exampleCN: 这份工作让他觉得受束缚。

items.meaning: the state of being shut in

items.example: They worked in a confined room.
items.exampleCN: 他们在一间狭小的房间里工作。

items.meaning: the outer limits of a place
items.example: He never left the confines of the town.
items.exampleCN: 他从未离开过这个镇的范围。

items.meaning: to mark out the exact meaning
items.exampleCN: 请把这个术语界定清楚。

definition_en: to show that something is true, or to make a plan or arrangement certain
core_image: 服务员在本子上把订位时间又圈了一遍
scene: 酒店前台打来电话，再次确认明天的房间。Please confirm your booking by email.
sceneCN: 这里 confirm 指「确认」（第 1 个义项：把已有安排再核实一遍）；句意是请通过邮件确认你的预订。

senses.title: Make an arrangement certain
senses.definition: to state that an arrangement is still true or will happen
senses.definitionCN: 说明某项安排仍然有效或将会发生
senses.example: Please confirm your booking by email.
senses.exampleCN: 请通过邮件确认你的预订。
senses.why: A plan spoken once can drift, and a second word pins it down.
senses.whyCN: 计划只说一次会飘走，再说一次才能把它钉住。

senses.title: Show that a fact is true
senses.definition: to provide evidence that a report or belief is correct
senses.definitionCN: 提供证据说明某个说法或想法是正确的
senses.example: The test confirmed his guess.
senses.exampleCN: 这次测试证实了他的猜测。
senses.why: Evidence turns a private guess into something others must accept.
senses.whyCN: 证据把私下的猜测变成别人必须接受的事实。

senses.title: Give official approval
senses.definition: to formally approve an appointment or decision
senses.definitionCN: 正式批准一项任命或决定
senses.example: The council confirmed the new plan.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会批准了新计划。
senses.why: A decision becomes final only when the proper body says yes.
senses.whyCN: 决定只有经有权机构点头，才算最终定下。

intro.en: Confirm comes from Latin confirmare, to make firm, built from com-, fully, and firmare, to strengthen.
intro.cn: confirm 来自拉丁语 confirmare，意为使坚固，由 com-（完全）与 firmare（加固）构成。

items.en: Firmus meant firm, steady and hard to move.
items.cn: firmus 意为坚固、稳定、难以推动。

items.en: Firmare meant to make something firm or secure.
items.cn: firmare 意为使某物坚固或牢靠。

items.en: Confirmare added com- to strengthen something completely.
items.cn: confirmare 加上 com-，表示把某物彻底加固。

items.en: Old French confermer carried the sense of making an agreement secure.
items.cn: 古法语 confermer 带有使约定变得牢靠的意思。

items.en: English confirm now means to prove true or to approve formally.
items.cn: 英语 confirm 如今指证明为真或正式批准。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that begin like confirm, and the meaning group names other ways of proving or approving.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 confirm 词形相近的词，近义组列出其他证明或批准的说法。

entries.definition: to behave in the way others expect
to keep within limits
to discuss or give an honour
to check that something is true
to show by evidence that something is true
to give formal approval to an agreement

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a circled time in a notebook, then move to a lab result and to a council vote.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从本子上被圈出的时间开始，再走到实验室结果与委员会表决。

normal.en: Con- is fully and firm means solid, so to confirm is to make a thing fully solid.
normal.cn: con- 是完全，firm 是坚固，所以 confirm 就是把一件事彻底坐实。

normal.en: A confirmed booking is a booking written in pen, not pencil.
normal.cn: 确认过的预订，是用钢笔而不是铅笔写下的预订。

normal.en: A test confirms a guess the way a key confirms a lock.
normal.cn: 测试证实猜测，正如钥匙印证了锁。

normal.en: To confirm a decision is to make it stand up and stop wobbling.
normal.cn: 批准一项决定，就是让它站稳、不再摇晃。

normal.en: Say it twice and check once more, and the fact is confirmed.
normal.cn: 说两遍再核对一次，事实就确认了。

abstract.en: Picture a pen drawing a second circle around a date.
abstract.cn: 想象一支笔在一个日期外又画了一圈。

abstract.en: Picture a stamp pressed down with both hands.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚印章被双手压下去。

abstract.en: Picture a nail driven fully into wood.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗钉子被完全敲进木头。

examples.en: Could you confirm the time of the meeting?
examples.cn: 你能确认一下会议时间吗？

examples.en: Later evidence confirmed her story.
examples.cn: 后来的证据证实了她的说法。

examples.en: The board confirmed him as the new director.
examples.cn: 董事会批准他为新任主管。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 confirm 记成 con（完全）加 firm（坚固）：把一件事彻底坐实、变得牢靠，就是确认与证实。

root: 源自拉丁语 confirmare（com 完全 + firmare 加固，源自 firmus 坚固），本义是使坚固，后引申为确认、证实与批准。

sensesIntro.en: From pinning down an arrangement, to proving a fact, and finally to giving official approval.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把安排钉牢，到证明一个事实，最后到给予正式批准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a date circled twice and a nail driven fully home.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个被圈了两遍的日期，一颗被完全敲进去的钉子。

branches.en: Confirming an arrangement removes the small doubt of a forgotten detail.
branches.cn: 确认安排，是消除「细节可能被忘」的小疑虑。

branches.en: Confirming a fact replaces belief with proof.
branches.cn: 证实事实，是用证据替换相信。

branches.en: Confirming a decision gives it the weight of an institution.
branches.cn: 批准决定，是给它加上机构的分量。

branches.en: Both senses make something stand firmer than before.
branches.cn: 两个义项都让某件事比原先站得更稳。

branches.en: Proof and approval both end a period of uncertainty.
branches.cn: 证实与批准都结束了一段不确定的时期。

intro.en: Confirm is built on Latin com-, fully, plus firmare, to make firm.
intro.cn: confirm 由拉丁语 com-（完全）与 firmare（使坚固）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin firm base also appears in firm, affirm and firmament.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的坚固词基 firm- 也出现在 firm、affirm 与 firmament 中。

items.exampleCN: 我们今天确认这份订单。

items.example: She is confirming the details now.

items.meaning: a statement that something is true
established and not likely to change
items.exampleCN: 他是一个坚定的支持者。
第二次测试是证实性的。

definition_en: a serious disagreement between people or groups, or a state of being opposed
core_image: 两股人马在窄路上迎面顶住，谁也不肯退
scene: 两个部门为了预算在会上争得面红耳赤。The conflict between the two teams slowed the project.
sceneCN: 这里 conflict 指「冲突」（第 1 个义项：双方之间的严重对立）；句意是两个团队之间的冲突拖慢了项目。

senses.title: A serious disagreement
senses.definition: a long or serious disagreement between people, groups or countries
senses.definitionCN: 个人、团体或国家之间长时间或严重的分歧
senses.example: The conflict lasted for many years.
senses.exampleCN: 这场冲突持续了许多年。
senses.why: Two sides want opposite things, and neither will step back.
senses.whyCN: 双方想要相反的东西，谁都不肯退让。

senses.title: A clash between ideas or rules
senses.definition: a situation where two ideas, rules or duties cannot both be true
senses.definitionCN: 两种想法、规则或职责无法同时成立的情形
senses.example: There is a conflict between the two rules.
senses.exampleCN: 这两条规则之间存在矛盾。
senses.why: A rule and a rule can fight just as two people can.
senses.whyCN: 规则与规则也会打架，就像两个人一样。

senses.title: To be opposed to
senses.definition: to be different from something in a way that cannot be reconciled
senses.definitionCN: 与某事物不同且无法调和
senses.example: His words conflict with his actions.
senses.exampleCN: 他的言语与行动相抵触。
senses.why: What is said and what is done can point in opposite directions.
senses.whyCN: 说的和做的，可能指向相反的方向。

intro.en: Conflict comes from Latin conflictus, a striking together, from confligere, to strike against.
intro.cn: conflict 来自拉丁语 conflictus，意为相互撞击，源自 confligere（彼此打击）。

items.en: Fligere meant to strike or knock something down.
items.cn: fligere 意为打击或击倒某物。

items.en: Confligere meant to strike two forces against each other.
items.cn: confligere 意为让两股力量彼此撞击。

items.en: Conflictus named the clash itself.
items.cn: conflictus 指撞击这件事本身。

items.en: French conflit carried the sense into disputes between people.
items.cn: 法语 conflit 把这个意思带入人与人之间的争端。

items.en: English conflict now covers war, argument and contradiction alike.
items.cn: 英语 conflict 如今同时覆盖战争、争吵与自相矛盾。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that end like conflict, and the meaning group names other kinds of clash.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 conflict 词尾相近的词，近义组列出其他表示冲突的说法。

entries.definition: to find someone guilty in court
to make something narrow or tight
to cause pain or trouble to someone
a serious argument about something
a short and sharp disagreement or fight
a hard fight to get or change something

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from two crowds meeting in a narrow lane, then move to two rules and to words that do not match actions.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从两群人在窄巷相遇开始，再走到两条规则与言行不一的场面。

normal.en: Con- is together and flict is strike, so conflict is two forces striking together.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，flict 是打击，所以 conflict 就是两股力量撞在一起。

normal.en: A conflict of interest means two duties want the same seat.
normal.cn: 利益冲突，就是两种职责抢同一把椅子。

normal.en: Armed conflict is the same clash with weapons added.
normal.cn: 武装冲突，就是同一个撞击加上了武器。

normal.en: Two rules in conflict cannot both be followed at once.
normal.cn: 两条相互抵触的规则，不可能同时遵守。

normal.en: When words conflict with actions, believe the actions.
normal.cn: 当言语与行动冲突时，相信行动。

abstract.en: Picture two waves breaking against each other.
abstract.cn: 想象两道浪迎面相撞。

abstract.en: Picture two arrows painted on one road.
abstract.cn: 想象同一条路上画着两支方向相反的箭头。

abstract.en: Picture two hands pushing one door from both sides.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手从两边推同一扇门。

examples.en: The two countries ended a long conflict.
examples.cn: 两国结束了一场长期冲突。

examples.en: There is a conflict between profit and safety.
examples.cn: 利润与安全之间存在矛盾。

examples.en: That rule conflicts with the older one.
examples.cn: 那条规则与旧规则相抵触。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 conflict 记成 con（一起）加 flict（打击）：两边一起动手互打，就是冲突；两条规则撞在一起，就是矛盾。

root: 源自拉丁语 conflictus（con 一起 + fligere 打击），本义是相互撞击，后引申为冲突、矛盾与抵触。

sensesIntro.en: From two forces striking, to two rules contradicting, and finally to words that do not match deeds.
sensesIntro.cn: 从两股力量相撞，到两条规则相悖，最后到言行对不上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two crowds meet in a narrow lane and neither will turn back.
core.cn: 核心意象：两群人在窄巷相遇，谁都不肯回头。

branches.en: The social sense is a clash between people with opposite aims.
branches.cn: 社会义项是目标相反的人之间的对撞。

branches.en: The logical sense is a clash between statements that cannot both hold.
branches.cn: 逻辑义项是两句不能同时成立的话之间的对撞。

branches.en: The verb sense describes the state of being opposed.
branches.cn: 动词义项描述彼此对立的状态。

branches.en: People and rules can both gridlock at a narrow point.
branches.cn: 人与规则都可能在狭窄处僵住。

branches.en: Contradiction and opposition are the same shape in different places.
branches.cn: 矛盾与对立，是同一种形状出现在不同地方。

intro.en: Conflict is built on Latin com-, together, plus fligere, to strike.
intro.cn: conflict 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 fligere（打击）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin strike base flict- also appears in inflict and afflict.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的打击词基 flict- 也出现在 inflict 与 afflict 中。

items.example: The region has seen many conflicts.
items.exampleCN: 这个地区经历过许多冲突。

items.example: Her duties conflicted with her wishes.
items.exampleCN: 她的职责与愿望发生了冲突。
我们收到了相互矛盾的报道。

items.meaning: not able to be true together
items.exampleCN: 这两个答案是彼此冲突的。
他对离开感到内心矛盾。
他们研究了一段充满冲突的关系。
暴风雨造成了严重破坏。

definition_zh: 使困惑；使糊涂；混淆；弄错
definition_en: to make someone unable to think clearly, or to mix two things up
core_image: 两条几乎一样的小路在雾里分成岔
scene: 新手看着两张几乎一样的表格，不知该填哪一张。Two similar forms confuse most new applicants.
sceneCN: 这里 confuse 指「使困惑」（第 1 个义项：让人弄不清该怎么办）；句意是两张相似的表格让大多数新申请者都糊涂了。

senses.title: Make someone unsure
senses.definition: to make someone unable to understand or decide
senses.definitionCN: 使人无法理解或无法作出决定
senses.example: The instructions confused everyone in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 这些说明让屋里每个人都糊涂了。
senses.why: Too many choices at once leave the mind without a path.
senses.whyCN: 选择一次给得太多，脑子就找不到一条路。

senses.title: Mix two things up
senses.definition: to mistake one person or thing for another
senses.definitionCN: 把一个人或一样东西误认成另一个
senses.example: People often confuse the two words.
senses.exampleCN: 人们常常把这两个词混淆。
senses.why: Two things that look alike are stored in the mind almost on the same shelf.
senses.whyCN: 长得像的两样东西，在脑中几乎摆在同一层架子上。

intro.en: Confuse comes from Latin confundere, to pour together, from com-, together, and fundere, to pour.
intro.cn: confuse 来自拉丁语 confundere，意为倒在一起，由 com-（一起）与 fundere（倾倒）构成。

items.en: Fundere meant to pour a liquid out of a container.
items.cn: fundere 意为把液体从容器里倒出来。

items.en: Confundere meant to pour several things into one vessel.
items.cn: confundere 意为把几样东西倒进同一个容器。

items.en: The mixed result was hard to separate again.
items.cn: 混在一起之后，就很难再分开。

items.en: Old French confondre used the image for a confused mind.
items.cn: 古法语 confondre 把这个意象用于混乱的心思。

items.en: English confuse now means to puzzle someone or to mix two things up.
items.cn: 英语 confuse 如今指使人困惑，或把两样东西混淆。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that begin like confuse, and the meaning group names other ways of puzzling someone.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 confuse 词形相近的词，近义组列出其他让人糊涂的说法。

entries.definition: to admit that you did something wrong
to face a problem or person directly
to say that you will not do something
to make someone think hard without an answer
to confuse someone completely
to give someone a wrong idea

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from two paths in fog, then move to two similar forms and to two words on one shelf.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从雾中的两条岔路开始，再走到两张相似的表格与同一层架子上的两个词。

normal.en: Con- is together and fuse is pour, so confuse is to pour everything into one cup.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，fuse 是倒，所以 confuse 就是把所有东西倒进一个杯子。

normal.en: A confused mind is a drawer where every sock has the same colour.
normal.cn: 困惑的脑子，就像一个里面每只袜子都同色的抽屉。

normal.en: To confuse two words is to give them one name by mistake.
normal.cn: 混淆两个词，就是误把它们当成同一个名字。

normal.en: Confusing instructions make a simple task look like a maze.
normal.cn: 令人费解的说明，把简单任务变成迷宫。

normal.en: The fog does not move the road; it only hides which road is which.
normal.cn: 雾没有移动道路，只是藏起了哪条是哪条。

abstract.en: Picture two roads splitting inside a grey fog.
abstract.cn: 想象两条路在灰雾中分开。

abstract.en: Picture two liquids meeting in one glass.
abstract.cn: 想象两种液体在同一只杯里相遇。

abstract.en: Picture two labels swapped on two jars.
abstract.cn: 想象两个罐子上的标签被互换。

examples.en: The map confused us more than it helped.
examples.cn: 这张地图没帮上忙，反而让我们更糊涂。

examples.en: Do not confuse being busy with being useful.
examples.cn: 不要把忙碌和有用混为一谈。

examples.en: Her sudden question confused the whole class.
examples.cn: 她突然的提问让全班都愣住了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 confuse 记成 con（一起）加 fuse（倒）：把好几样东西倒进一个杯子搅在一起，人就分不清了，这就是使困惑与混淆。

root: 源自拉丁语 confundere（com 一起 + fundere 倾倒），本义是倒在一起，后引申为使困惑、混淆与搅乱。

sensesIntro.en: From several liquids poured into one cup, to a mind that cannot tell two things apart.
sensesIntro.cn: 从几种液体倒进一只杯子，到一颗分不清两样东西的脑袋。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two roads vanish into fog and two labels sit on the wrong jars.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条路消失在雾里，两个标签贴错了罐子。

branches.en: Being confused is a state of not knowing which way to go.
branches.cn: 困惑就是不知道往哪边走的状态。

branches.en: Confusing two things means giving one the name of the other.
branches.cn: 混淆两样东西，就是把一个的名字给了另一个。

branches.en: Both senses come from a boundary that has stopped being visible.
branches.cn: 两个义项都来自一条已经看不见的界线。

branches.en: Clear steps are the best cure for a confused mind.
branches.cn: 清楚的步骤是治困惑最好的药。

branches.en: Look-alike words are the easiest pair to confuse.
branches.cn: 长得像的词，是最容易被混淆的一对。

intro.en: Confuse is built on Latin com-, together, plus fundere, to pour.
intro.cn: confuse 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 fundere（倾倒）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pour base fus- also appears in refuse, fusion and suffuse.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的倾倒词基 fus- 也出现在 refuse、fusion 与 suffuse 中。

items.example: Do not confuse the two labels.
items.exampleCN: 不要把这两个标签弄混。
这个回答把我弄糊涂了。

items.example: The room was full of confusion.
She looked confused by the question.
items.exampleCN: 她似乎被这个问题问住了。

items.example: They refuse to change the date.

definition_en: a state of not understanding what is happening, or a lack of order
core_image: 雾中的一群人，各朝不同的方向走
scene: 停电之后，大厅里的人不知该往哪个出口走。The sudden darkness caused confusion in the hall.
sceneCN: 这里 confusion 指「混乱」（第 2 个义项：秩序被打乱的状态）；句意是突然的黑暗在大厅里引起了混乱。

senses.title: A puzzled mind
senses.definition: the feeling of not being able to understand or decide
senses.definitionCN: 无法理解或无法决定的感受
senses.example: His answer left me in complete confusion.
senses.exampleCN: 他的回答让我完全糊涂了。
senses.why: A mind given too many directions at once stops choosing any.
senses.whyCN: 脑子同时收到太多方向，就一个也不选了。

senses.title: A lack of order
senses.definition: a situation in which things are disordered and hard to control
senses.definitionCN: 事物秩序被打乱、难以控制的情形
senses.example: The room was in complete confusion after the move.
senses.exampleCN: 搬完之后房间里一片混乱。
senses.why: When every object leaves its place, the eye loses its map.
senses.whyCN: 每样东西都离开原位，眼睛就失去了地图。

senses.title: Mixing two things up
senses.definition: the act of treating two different things as the same
senses.definitionCN: 把两样不同的事物当成同一样
senses.example: The confusion of the two names caused real trouble.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个名称的混淆带来了真正的麻烦。
senses.why: A name is a handle, and two handles on one door lead to the wrong room.
senses.whyCN: 名字是把手，一扇门上装两个把手就会走错房间。

intro.en: Confusion comes from Latin confusio, a pouring together, from confundere, to pour together.
intro.cn: confusion 来自拉丁语 confusio，意为倒在一起，源自 confundere（混合倾倒）。

items.en: Fundere meant to pour something out.
items.cn: fundere 意为把某物倒出来。

items.en: Confundere meant to pour different things into one container.
items.cn: confundere 意为把不同的东西倒进同一个容器。

items.en: Confusio named the mixed and disordered result.
items.cn: confusio 指混合之后那种杂乱的结果。

items.en: French confusion applied the image to a disordered mind.
items.cn: 法语 confusion 把这个意象用于混乱的心思。

items.en: English confusion now covers puzzlement, disorder and mistaken identity.
items.cn: 英语 confusion 如今覆盖困惑、混乱与认错对象。

note.en: The look-alike group holds nouns with a similar ending, and the meaning group names other states of disorder or doubt.
note.cn: 形近组收的是词尾相近的名词，近义组列出其他表示混乱或疑惑的状态。

entries.definition: a judgement reached after thinking
a statement admitting a fault
something given up in an argument
a state in which things are not properly arranged
a state of complete and confusing disorder
the feeling of being unable to understand

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a crowd walking in different directions, then move to a moved room and to two names on one door.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从各走各的人群开始，再走到刚搬完的房间与一扇门上的两个名字。

normal.en: Confuse plus -ion turns the act of mixing into the state of being mixed.
normal.cn: confuse 加 -ion，就把混合的动作变成了混合的状态。

normal.en: Confusion is what a room looks like when every chair has forgotten its corner.
normal.cn: 混乱，就是每把椅子都忘了自己该在哪个角落的房间。

normal.en: A crowd in confusion moves fast and arrives nowhere.
normal.cn: 混乱中的人群走得很快，却哪里也到不了。

normal.en: The confusion of two names is a small mistake with a long shadow.
normal.cn: 两个名字的混淆是小错，却拖着长长的影子。

normal.en: Clear one fact at a time, and confusion begins to thin.
normal.cn: 一次弄清一个事实，混乱就开始变薄。

abstract.en: Picture a fog full of people facing different ways.
abstract.cn: 想象一片雾里的人群面朝不同方向。

abstract.en: Picture a desk swept into one pile.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子被扫成一堆。

abstract.en: Picture two names written on one door.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门上写着两个名字。

examples.en: There was some confusion about the meeting time.
examples.cn: 关于会议时间有一些混乱。

examples.en: The new signs should clear up the confusion.
examples.cn: 新标志应该能消除这种困惑。

examples.en: In the confusion, nobody noticed the open gate.
examples.cn: 在一片混乱中，没人注意到敞开的大门。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 confusion 记成 confuse（倒在一起）加 ion：东西全倒在一处，分不清彼此，就是混乱与困惑。

root: 源自拉丁语 confusio（con 一起 + fundere 倾倒），本义是混倒在一起，后引申为困惑、混乱与混淆。

sensesIntro.en: From liquids mixed in one vessel, to a mind without direction, and finally to two things taken for one.
sensesIntro.cn: 从倒进同一容器的液体，到失去方向的头脑，最后到把两样东西当成一样。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foggy hall where everyone walks a different way.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片雾中的大厅，每个人走向不同方向。

branches.en: The mental sense is a person who cannot decide.
branches.cn: 心理义项是一个无法做决定的人。

branches.en: The physical sense is a space that has lost its order.
branches.cn: 物理义项是一个失去秩序的空间。

branches.en: The naming sense is two different things sharing one label.
branches.cn: 命名义项是两样不同的东西共用同一个标签。

branches.en: A disordered room and a disordered mind look surprisingly alike.
branches.cn: 杂乱的房间与杂乱的头脑，看起来出奇地像。

branches.en: Mixing up names is the smallest form of a larger mess.
branches.cn: 弄混名字，是更大混乱中最小的那一种。

intro.en: Confusion is Latin com-, together, plus fundere, to pour, with the noun ending -ion.
intro.cn: confusion 由拉丁语 com-（一起）、fundere（倾倒）与名词词尾 -ion 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pour base fus- also appears in fusion and refuse.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的倾倒词基 fus- 也出现在 fusion 与 refuse 中。

items.meaning: a state of disorder or doubt
items.exampleCN: 这个消息引起了很大的混乱。
这两张地图让旅行者犯糊涂。
每个人看上去都很困惑。

items.meaning: the joining of two things into one
items.example: The band plays a fusion of jazz and folk.
items.exampleCN: 这支乐队演奏爵士与民谣的融合。

items.example: She refused to sign the form.
A warm light suffused the room.
items.exampleCN: 温暖的光弥漫了整个房间。

definition_en: words that praise someone for a success or a happy event
core_image: 亲友围上来，举杯对刚拿到证书的人说恭喜
scene: 毕业典礼散场后，亲友围住拿着证书的年轻人道贺。His congratulation was just one word, but it meant a lot.
sceneCN: 这里 congratulation 指「祝贺的话」（第 1 个义项：对成功或喜事的称贺）；句意是他这一句祝贺虽短，分量却很重。

senses.title: Words of praise
senses.definition: praise spoken to someone who has done well
senses.definitionCN: 对做得好的人说出的称赞话
senses.example: Please accept my congratulation on your success.
senses.exampleCN: 请接受我对你成功的祝贺。
senses.why: A good deed deserves a voice that names it out loud.
senses.whyCN: 一件好事值得有人大声说出来。

senses.title: The plural greeting
senses.definition: the plural form used as a warm greeting on happy events
senses.definitionCN: 复数形式，用于喜事场合的热情祝贺
senses.example: Congratulations! You passed the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 恭喜！你考试通过了。
senses.why: A happy event is often too big for one word, so English doubles it.
senses.whyCN: 喜事往往一句话装不下，所以英语把它说成复数。

intro.en: Congratulation comes from Latin congratulari, to wish joy together, built from com-, together, and gratulari, to show joy.
intro.cn: congratulation 来自拉丁语 congratulari，意为一起道喜，由 com-（一起）与 gratulari（表达喜悦）构成。

items.en: Gratulari meant to show joy or give thanks out loud.
items.cn: gratulari 意为把喜悦或感谢说出口。

items.en: Congratulari added com- to make the joy a shared act.
items.cn: congratulari 加上 com-，让这份喜悦成为共同的行动。

items.en: The noun congratulatio named the act of shared rejoicing.
items.cn: 名词 congratulatio 指共同欢庆的行为。

items.en: French carried the word into polite speech at court.
items.cn: 法语把这个词带进宫廷里的礼貌用语。

items.en: English congratulation first meant a public expression of joy.
items.cn: 英语 congratulation 最初指公开表达喜悦。

items.en: It now appears mostly in the plural as a warm greeting.
items.cn: 如今它多以复数形式出现，用作热情的问候。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words built on the same Latin thanks base, and the meaning group names other kinds of spoken praise.
note.cn: 形近组收的是建立在同一个拉丁语感谢词基上的词，近义组列出其他表示口头称赞的说法。

entries.definition: to tell someone you are happy about their success
expressing good wishes for someone
the ceremony of receiving a degree
words that say someone or something is good
a polite remark that admires someone

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a room full of one good word, then move to the doubled plural and to the right moment.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一间满是同一句好话的屋子开始，再走到复数的叠用与恰当的时机。

normal.en: Con- is together and grat- is thanks, so congratulation is thanks spoken together.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，grat- 是感谢，congratulation 就是大家一起说出的感谢。

normal.en: A wedding hall full of one good word: that is congratulation.
normal.cn: 整个婚礼大厅说着同一句好话，那就是祝贺。

normal.en: One word of praise is small, so English often doubles it into congratulations.
normal.cn: 一句称赞太轻，所以英语常把它说成复数的 congratulations。

normal.en: A short congratulation at the right moment beats a long letter a week later.
normal.cn: 关键时刻一句简短祝贺，胜过一周后的一封长信。

normal.en: Say it while the good news is still warm.
normal.cn: 趁好消息还热着的时候把它说出口。

abstract.en: Picture a cup lifted toward a smiling face.
abstract.cn: 想象一只杯子朝一张笑脸举起来。

abstract.en: Picture one word written on a card and handed across a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词写在卡片上，隔着桌子递过去。

abstract.en: Picture a room where every hand claps at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子里所有的手同时拍响。

examples.en: She sent a short congratulation to the whole team.
examples.cn: 她给整个团队发了一句简短的祝贺。

examples.en: Congratulations on your new job!
examples.cn: 祝贺你找到新工作！

examples.en: His congratulation sounded formal but honest.
examples.cn: 他的祝贺听起来正式，却很真诚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 congratulation 记成 con（一起）加 grat（感谢）：一群人一起把感谢说出口，就是祝贺。

root: 源自拉丁语 congratulari（com 一起 + gratulari 表达喜悦），本义是一起道喜，后指祝贺的话与贺词。

sensesIntro.en: From one spoken word of praise to the doubled plural that a whole room says at a wedding.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一句说出口的称赞，到婚礼上整间屋子齐声说出的复数祝贺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circle of people lifting cups and saying one good word.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈人举起杯子，说着同一句好话。

branches.en: A single congratulation is a spoken gift for a success.
branches.cn: 一句祝贺，是送给成功者的口头礼物。

branches.en: The plural form turns one word into a small round of applause.
branches.cn: 复数形式把一个词变成一小阵掌声。

branches.en: Both senses need a listener who has just done something worth naming.
branches.cn: 两种义项都需要一个刚做成某事的听者。

branches.en: At weddings and graduations the plural is the normal greeting.
branches.cn: 在婚礼与毕业典礼上，复数形式才是常规问候。

branches.en: The word marks a moment, and the moment makes the word warm.
branches.cn: 这个词标记一个时刻，而这个时刻让这个词变暖。

intro.en: Congratulation is built on Latin com-, together, plus gratulari, to show joy.
intro.cn: congratulation 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 gratulari（表达喜悦）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin thanks base grat- also appears in gratitude, grateful and gratify.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的感谢词基 grat- 也出现在 gratitude、grateful 与 gratify 中。

items.meaning: the act of wishing joy to someone
items.example: Their congratulation came before the cake.
items.exampleCN: 他们的祝贺在蛋糕端上来之前就到了。

items.meaning: to speak praise to someone for a success
items.example: We congratulated her on the prize.

items.meaning: a warm greeting on a happy event

items.example: The news gratified the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个消息让全家人都很欣慰。
她说话时带着真诚的感激。

items.example: I am grateful for your help.

items.exampleCN: 他用忘恩负义回报善意。

definition_en: to join two things together, or to see how they are related
core_image: 两根电线被拧在一起，灯泡立刻亮起
scene: 电工蹲在配电箱前，把两根电线接妥。Connect the red wire to the blue one.
sceneCN: 这里 connect 指「连接」（第 1 个义项：把两物接在一起）；句意是把红线接到蓝线上。

senses.title: Join two things
senses.definition: to join two objects so that they touch or work together
senses.definitionCN: 把两个物体接在一起，使之接触或共同运作
senses.example: Connect the printer to the computer.
senses.exampleCN: 把打印机接到电脑上。
senses.why: Two loose ends become one working line at the moment they touch.
senses.whyCN: 两个松开的端点一碰，就变成一条能工作的线。

senses.title: See a link
senses.definition: to realize that two facts or people are related
senses.definitionCN: 意识到两件事或两个人之间存在关联
senses.example: She connected the smell with her grandmother's kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那股气味和祖母的厨房联系起来。
senses.why: The mind ties two memories with the same quiet thread.
senses.whyCN: 头脑用同一根安静的线，把两段记忆系在一起。

senses.title: Join a network
senses.definition: to join a phone or computer network, or to make a route open
senses.definitionCN: 接入电话或计算机网络，或使线路开通
senses.example: The call failed to connect.
senses.exampleCN: 电话没有接通。
senses.why: A network is only useful when your line reaches the others.
senses.whyCN: 网络只有在你这条线接到别人那里时才有用。

intro.en: Connect comes from Latin connectere, to bind together, from com-, together, and nectere, to tie.
intro.cn: connect 来自拉丁语 connectere，意为绑在一起，由 com-（一起）与 nectere（系、绑）构成。

items.en: Nectere meant to tie or bind one thing to another.
items.cn: nectere 意为把一物系到另一物上。

items.en: Connectere added com- to make the binding mutual.
items.cn: connectere 加上 com-，表示彼此相系。

items.en: Connexus was the participle, already tied into one.
items.cn: connexus 是它的分词形式，已经系成一体。

items.en: French connecter carried the tying sense into daily use.
items.cn: 法语 connecter 把这个系绑的含义带入日常使用。

items.en: English connect first meant to fasten two things physically.
items.cn: 英语 connect 最初指把两件东西在物理上固定在一起。

items.en: It now covers wires, ideas, people and networks.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖电线、想法、人与网络。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the shape of connect, and the meaning group names other ways to hold two things together.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 connect 外形相近的词，近义组列出其他把两物连在一起的说法。

entries.definition: to bring things together from different places
right and without mistakes
the older British spelling of connection
to join two things or ideas
to fasten one thing to another
to join together into one whole

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a knot that binds two ends, then move to wires and finally to a link inside the mind.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一个把两端系住的结开始，再到电线，最后到头脑里的联想。

normal.en: Con- is together and nect- is bind, so connect is to bind two things into one.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，nect- 是绑，connect 就是把两样东西绑成一体。

normal.en: Think of a knot in a shoelace: two ends, one line.
normal.cn: 想想鞋带上的一个结：两个端头，一条线。

normal.en: A charger cable connects the wall to the phone.
normal.cn: 充电线把墙壁和手机连接起来。

normal.en: Connecting the dots means letting one fact lead to another.
normal.cn: 把线索串起来，就是让一件事引出另一件事。

normal.en: If the call does not connect, the line stays silent.
normal.cn: 电话若接不通，线路就始终沉默。

abstract.en: Picture two bare wires touching in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象两根裸露的电线在黑暗里碰在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a thread pulled tight between two beads.
abstract.cn: 想象一根线在两颗珠子之间被拉紧。

abstract.en: Picture two lamps lighting up at the same instant.
abstract.cn: 想象两盏灯在同一瞬间亮起。

examples.en: Connect the cable to the socket first.
examples.cn: 先把电缆接到插座上。

examples.en: At first I did not connect the two events.
examples.cn: 起初我并没有把这两件事联系起来。

examples.en: This road connects the village with the highway.
examples.cn: 这条路把村庄和高速公路连起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 connect 记成 con（一起）加 nect（绑）：把两端绑到一起，就是连接，也指把人和事联系起来。

root: 源自拉丁语 connectere（com 一起 + nectere 系绑），本义是绑在一起，后引申为连接、联系与接通。

sensesIntro.en: From two wires tied into one line, to two memories tied in the mind, and finally to a line reaching a network.
sensesIntro.cn: 从两根电线接成一条线，到两段记忆在脑中相连，最后到线路接入网络。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two loose ends twisted into one working line.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个松开的端头被拧成一条能工作的线。

branches.en: The first sense is the physical joining of two objects.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是两个物体在物理上的接合。

branches.en: The second sense joins ideas rather than objects.
branches.cn: 第二个义项连接的是想法而不是物体。

branches.en: The third sense opens a channel to a larger system.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是向更大的系统打开一条通道。

branches.en: A wire and a network both need a point where the line meets.
branches.cn: 电线与网络都需要一个线路相接的节点。

branches.en: Hands join objects, and the mind joins what the objects mean.
branches.cn: 手把物体接起来，头脑把物体的含义接起来。

intro.en: Connect is built on Latin com-, together, plus nectere, to bind.
intro.cn: connect 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 nectere（系绑）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin bind base nect- also appears in annex and nexus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的系绑词基 nect- 也出现在 annex 与 nexus 中。

items.exampleCN: 在这里把两根管子接上。

items.meaning: a part that joins two devices

items.exampleCN: 这个镇把那片农田并了进来。

items.example: The port is a nexus of trade.
items.exampleCN: 这个港口是贸易的枢纽。

definition_zh: 连接；联系；关系；转乘衔接；人脉
definition_en: the state of being joined, a relationship, or a transport link that lets you continue a journey
core_image: 一张网把散落的点一格一格连起来
scene: 火车晚点，年轻人冲上月台时车门刚好关上。I missed the connection by two minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 connection 指「转乘衔接」（第 3 个义项：交通工具之间的接续）；句意是我差两分钟没赶上换乘。

senses.title: Being joined
senses.definition: the state of two things being joined together
senses.definitionCN: 两件东西被接在一起的状态
senses.example: Check the connection between the pipe and the tank.
senses.exampleCN: 检查一下管道和水箱之间的连接。
senses.why: Two parts stop being separate once a joint holds them.
senses.whyCN: 一旦有了接头把两部分固定住，它们就不再彼此分开。

senses.title: A relationship
senses.definition: a relationship between people, things or ideas, including people you know
senses.definitionCN: 人、事物或想法之间的关系，也包括认识的人
senses.example: There is a clear connection between smoking and heart disease.
senses.exampleCN: 吸烟与心脏病之间有明显的联系。
senses.why: A link that cannot be seen still pulls two facts toward each other.
senses.whyCN: 看不见的联系，仍然会把两件事实拉在一起。

senses.title: A travel link
senses.definition: a bus, train or flight that lets you continue a journey
senses.definitionCN: 让你继续行程的接驳车、火车或航班
senses.example: The flight was late, so I missed my connection.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机晚点，所以我错过了转乘。
senses.why: One vehicle hands you to another, and the journey stays unbroken.
senses.whyCN: 一个交通工具把你交给另一个，行程因此不断。

intro.en: Connection comes from Latin connexio, a binding together, from connectere, to tie, and was spelled with an x for centuries.
intro.cn: connection 来自拉丁语 connexio，意为绑在一起，源自动词 connectere（系绑），有几个世纪都写作 x 的拼法。

items.en: Nectere meant to tie, and connectere meant to tie together.
items.cn: nectere 意为系绑，connectere 意为绑在一起。

items.en: Connexio named the joint or the act of binding.
items.cn: connexio 指接合处或绑缚的行为。

items.en: Old French connexion kept the x of the Latin participle.
items.cn: 古法语 connexion 保留了拉丁语分词里的 x。

items.en: English took the word as connexion and used it for any join.
items.cn: 英语以 connexion 的形式借入，用来指任何连接。

items.en: Writers began to spell it connection to match the Latin verb.
items.cn: 写作者开始把它拼作 connection，以贴合拉丁动词。

items.en: Connection is now standard, and it also means a train or flight link.
items.cn: 如今 connection 是标准拼法，也指火车或航班的接续。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that echo the sound or shape of connection, and the meaning group names other kinds of link.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 connection 音形相近的词，近义组列出其他表示联系的说法。

entries.definition: the older British spelling of connection
a change that makes something right
a group of things gathered together
a relationship or a joining part
the way two people or things are connected
a strong tie between people

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from two dots joined by a line, then move to people who know each other and to two trains meeting on a platform.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从两个被一条线连起来的点开始，再到彼此认识的人，最后到月台上相接的两趟列车。

normal.en: Con- is together, nect- is bind, and -ion makes it a thing, so a connection is a binding.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，nect- 是绑，-ion 把它变成名词，所以 connection 就是一次绑缚。

normal.en: Two dots and one line: that is the whole picture.
normal.cn: 两个点加一条线，整幅画面就是这些。

normal.en: A bad connection makes a voice break into pieces.
normal.cn: 连接不好时，说话声会碎成一片片。

normal.en: Some connections are people: a friend who knows a friend.
normal.cn: 有些 connection 指的是人：朋友的朋友。

normal.en: A missed connection leaves you standing while the train leaves.
normal.cn: 错过转乘，就只能站着看火车开走。

abstract.en: Picture two islands with one rope stretched between them.
abstract.cn: 想象两座岛之间拉着一根绳。

abstract.en: Picture a handshake that lasts a whole career.
abstract.cn: 想象一次握手支撑起整个职业生涯。

abstract.en: Picture a platform clock showing the same minute twice.
abstract.cn: 想象站台时钟两次指到同一分钟。

examples.en: The connection between diet and mood is well known.
examples.cn: 饮食与情绪之间的联系广为人知。

examples.en: He has good connections in the publishing world.
examples.cn: 他在出版界有很好的人脉。

examples.en: I have a connection in Paris, so the trip takes two flights.
examples.cn: 我要在巴黎转机，所以这趟行程要坐两班飞机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 connection 记成 con（一起）加 nect（绑）加 ion（名词）：绑在一起的结果，就是连接，也可以指人与人之间的门路。

root: 源自拉丁语 connexio（com 一起 + nectere 系绑），本义是绑在一起，后引申为联系、关系、人脉与交通接续。

sensesIntro.en: From a physical joint, to a relationship between facts or people, and finally to a train or flight that carries you onward.
sensesIntro.cn: 从物理上的接头，到事实或人之间的关系，最后到把你继续送走的火车或航班。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two points apart, joined by one taut line.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个分开的点，被一条绷紧的线连起来。

branches.en: The basic sense is a joint where two parts hold together.
branches.cn: 基本义项是两部分相互固定的接头。

branches.en: The link can be invisible yet still tie facts or people.
branches.cn: 这种联系可以看不见，却仍然把事实或人系在一起。

branches.en: In travel, the link is a vehicle that takes over from another.
branches.cn: 在旅途中，这一环是从另一班接手的交通工具。

branches.en: Both a wire and a friendship need two ends that stay in place.
branches.cn: 电线与友情都需要两端各自守在原处。

branches.en: A good contact at an airport is a personal connection and a flight link at once.
branches.cn: 机场里的熟人，同时是人脉与航班接续。

intro.en: Connection is built on Latin com-, together, plus nectere, to bind, with the noun ending -ion.
intro.cn: connection 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 nectere（系绑）加上名词词尾 -ion 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin bind base nect- also appears in nexus and annex, and its participle gave the x spelling connexio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的系绑词基 nect- 也出现在 nexus 与 annex 中，其分词形式带来了 connexio 的 x 拼法。

items.meaning: the state or act of being joined
items.exampleCN: 这个接头在压力下没有松脱。
结缔组织支撑着这个器官。

items.meaning: a piece that links two devices

items.exampleCN: 这些事件彼此密切相关。

items.meaning: the same word in its older British form
items.meaningCN: 同一个词的旧式英式写法

items.example: The station is a nexus of the city.
items.exampleCN: 这座车站是城市的枢纽。

definition_zh: 有意识的；清醒的；察觉到的；刻意的
definition_en: awake and able to think, aware of something, or done on purpose
core_image: 病房里，病人睁开眼，第一次看清天花板
scene: 病人睁眼后先看清天花板，再认出床边的人。She was conscious of every sound in the room.
sceneCN: 这里 conscious 指「察觉到的」（第 2 个义项：意识到某事存在）；句意是她察觉到房间里的每一种声音。

pos.zh: 有意识的；清醒的；察觉的；刻意的

senses.title: Awake and aware
senses.definition: awake and able to think and feel
senses.definitionCN: 醒着，能够思考与感受
senses.example: The patient was conscious after the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 手术之后病人是清醒的。
senses.why: The light is on behind the eyes again.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛后面的灯，又亮起来了。

senses.title: Noticing something
senses.definition: noticing that something exists or is happening
senses.definitionCN: 注意到某事物的存在或正在发生
senses.example: She was conscious of every sound in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 她察觉到房间里的每一种声音。
senses.why: Attention turns a background noise into a fact you must answer.
senses.whyCN: 注意力把背景里的声音，变成你必须回应的事实。

senses.title: Done on purpose
senses.definition: deliberate and intended rather than accidental
senses.definitionCN: 有意为之，而非偶然发生
senses.example: He made a conscious effort to slow down.
senses.exampleCN: 他刻意放慢了速度。
senses.why: A choice you can see yourself making is a choice you own.
senses.whyCN: 你能看见自己做出的选择，才是你真正拥有的选择。

intro.en: Conscious comes from Latin conscius, knowing with others or within oneself, from com-, with, and scire, to know.
intro.cn: conscious 来自拉丁语 conscius，意为与他人或与自己共知，由 com-（与）与 scire（知道）构成。

items.en: Scire meant to know, and conscius meant sharing that knowledge.
items.cn: scire 意为知道，conscius 意为共享这份知识。

items.en: A conscious person was one who knew a thing with another.
items.cn: conscius 的人，是与另一个人共同知道某事的人。

items.en: Later the knowing turned inward, meaning aware of oneself.
items.cn: 后来这种知道转向内部，表示对自身的察觉。

items.en: English conscious first meant sharing knowledge of something.
items.cn: 英语 conscious 最初指对某事知情。

items.en: It settled into the modern sense of awake and aware.
items.cn: 它逐渐固定为清醒而有察觉的现代含义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the conscience family, and the meaning group names other words for being aware or deliberate.
note.cn: 形近组是 conscience 家族，近义组列出其他表示察觉或刻意的词。

entries.definition: the inner sense of right and wrong
the state of being awake and aware
careful to do things properly
knowing that something exists
not asleep
done on purpose

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from eyes opening in a hospital bed, then move to a sound you cannot ignore and to a step you choose to take.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从病床上睁开的眼睛开始，再到无法忽略的声音，最后到你选择迈出的一步。

normal.en: Con- is with and sci- is know, so conscious is knowing with your own mind.
normal.cn: con- 是与，sci- 是知道，conscious 就是用自己的心智去知道。

normal.en: Waking up is the first conscious moment of the day.
normal.cn: 醒来，是一天中第一个有意识的时刻。

normal.en: To be conscious of a sound is to let it into your mind.
normal.cn: 察觉到一种声音，就是让它进入你的头脑。

normal.en: A conscious choice leaves a footprint you can point to.
normal.cn: 有意的选择，会留下一个你能指出的脚印。

normal.en: Half awake is not conscious enough to drive.
normal.cn: 半睡半醒，还没清醒到可以开车。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp switching on above a bed.
abstract.cn: 想象床头上方一盏灯被打开。

abstract.en: Picture a finger lifted to say wait a moment.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指举起来，示意稍等。

abstract.en: Picture a foot placed slowly and on purpose.
abstract.cn: 想象一只脚缓慢而刻意地落下。

examples.en: He was conscious during the whole flight.
examples.cn: 整个飞行途中他都是清醒的。

examples.en: I am conscious of my own limits.
examples.cn: 我清楚自己的限度。

examples.en: She made a conscious choice to stay.
examples.cn: 她是有意选择留下来的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 conscious 记成 con（与自己一起）加 sci（知道）加 ous（形容词）：心里明白自己与周围在发生什么，就是有意识。

root: 源自拉丁语 conscius（com 与 + scire 知道），本义是共知，后转为对自身与周围有察觉，并引申出刻意的含义。

sensesIntro.en: From eyes opening, to a sound entering the mind, and finally to a step taken on purpose.
sensesIntro.cn: 从眼睛睁开，到声音进入头脑，最后到刻意迈出的一步。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp switched on behind the eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：眼睛后面有一盏灯被点亮。

branches.en: The first sense is simply being awake and able to think.
branches.cn: 第一个义项只是醒着并能思考。

branches.en: The second sense points outward at something noticed.
branches.cn: 第二个义项目光向外，指向被注意到的事物。

branches.en: The third sense turns awareness into a chosen act.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把觉察变成有意的行动。

branches.en: You must be awake before anything can be noticed.
branches.cn: 必须先醒着，才可能注意到什么。

branches.en: Noticing a habit is the first step to changing it on purpose.
branches.cn: 察觉一个习惯，是刻意改变它的第一步。

intro.en: Conscious is built on Latin com-, with, plus scire, to know, and the adjective ending -ous.
intro.cn: conscious 由拉丁语 com-（与）与 scire（知道）加上形容词词尾 -ous 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin know base sci- also appears in science, conscience and omniscient.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的知道词基 sci- 也出现在 science、conscience 与 omniscient 中。

items.exampleCN: 药物让他的意识变得迟钝。

items.example: He was unconscious on the floor.
items.exampleCN: 他倒在地板上失去了知觉。

items.example: A subconscious habit shaped her choice.
items.exampleCN: 一个潜意识习惯塑造了她的选择。

items.meaning: the inner sense of right and wrong

items.exampleCN: 没有哪位老师无所不知。

definition_en: the state of being awake and able to think, or awareness of a shared issue
core_image: 麻醉退去，天花板的灯光一点点变清晰
scene: 麻醉慢慢退去，病人终于认出病房里的窗帘。He lost consciousness for a few seconds.
sceneCN: 这里 consciousness 指「知觉」（第 2 个义项：清醒并感知外界的状态）；句意是他有几秒钟失去了知觉。

senses.title: Being awake
senses.definition: the state of being awake and able to think and feel
senses.definitionCN: 醒着并能思考、感受的状态
senses.example: He slowly regained consciousness in the ambulance.
senses.exampleCN: 他在救护车里慢慢恢复了知觉。
senses.why: The inner light goes out, and then it comes back.
senses.whyCN: 心里的灯先熄灭，然后又亮起来。

senses.title: Awareness of something
senses.definition: the fact of noticing or caring about an issue
senses.definitionCN: 对某个问题的注意与关心
senses.example: There is growing consciousness of water waste.
senses.exampleCN: 人们对水资源浪费的意识正在增强。
senses.why: A problem becomes real to a person only when it is noticed.
senses.whyCN: 一个问题被人注意到，才对这个人变得真实。

senses.title: A shared mindset
senses.definition: the shared beliefs and feelings of a group
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体共有的信念与感受
senses.example: The movement changed public consciousness.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动改变了公众意识。
senses.why: Many private minds can settle into one common weather.
senses.whyCN: 许多私人的心思，可以沉淀成一种共同的天气。

intro.en: Consciousness is conscious plus the noun ending -ness, built on Latin conscius, knowing with oneself.
intro.cn: consciousness 是 conscious 加名词词尾 -ness，源头是拉丁语 conscius，意为与自己共知。

items.en: Scire meant to know, and conscius meant sharing knowledge.
items.cn: scire 意为知道，conscius 意为共享知识。

items.en: The noun conscientia named inward knowledge of oneself.
items.cn: 名词 conscientia 指对自身的内部知识。

items.en: English formed consciousness from conscious and -ness.
items.cn: 英语用 conscious 加 -ness 造出 consciousness。

items.en: Psychology made it the name of the waking mind.
items.cn: 心理学把它定为清醒心智的名称。

items.en: It now also means a group's shared awareness of an issue.
items.cn: 如今它也指一个群体对某个问题的共同意识。

note.en: The look-alike group is the conscience family, and the meaning group names other states of noticing.
note.cn: 形近组是 conscience 家族，近义组列出其他表示察觉状态的词。

entries.definition: the inner sense of right and wrong
awake and aware
careful to do what is right
knowledge that something exists
the state of being quick to notice
the part of a person that thinks and feels

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a waking patient, then move to a problem people begin to see and to a mood shared by a crowd.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从醒来的病人开始，再到人们开始看见的问题，最后到人群共有的情绪。

normal.en: Conscious plus -ness is simply the state of being conscious.
normal.cn: conscious 加 -ness，就是处于有意识状态。

normal.en: Losing consciousness is a light going out; regaining it is the switch clicking back.
normal.cn: 失去知觉是灯灭了，恢复知觉是开关又咔哒一声。

normal.en: Social consciousness begins when a private worry becomes a public word.
normal.cn: 社会意识始于私人的担忧变成一个公开的词。

normal.en: A raised consciousness is a raised hand.
normal.cn: 被唤醒的觉悟，就是一只举起来的手。

normal.en: The word sounds like conscience but points at the light, not the judge.
normal.cn: 这个词听起来像 conscience，但它指那盏灯，而不是法官。

abstract.en: Picture a white ceiling slowly coming into focus.
abstract.cn: 想象白色的天花板慢慢变清晰。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd all turning to look at one sign.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人同时转头看同一块牌子。

abstract.en: Picture a hand held up in a dark hall.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗大厅里举起的一只手。

examples.en: The blow did not cost him consciousness.
examples.cn: 那一击没有让他失去知觉。

examples.en: Environmental consciousness has grown in the past decade.
examples.cn: 环保意识在过去十年里增强了。

examples.en: She spoke with a new consciousness of her own rights.
examples.cn: 她带着对自身权利的新觉悟说话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 consciousness 记成 conscious（有意识的）加 ness（状态）：灯亮着的那种状态，就是意识。

root: 由拉丁语 conscius（com 与 + scire 知道）经 conscious 加 -ness 构成，指清醒感知的状态，后扩展为群体觉悟。

sensesIntro.en: From the light of a waking mind, to noticing a problem, and finally to a belief shared by many.
sensesIntro.cn: 从清醒心智的光，到注意到某个问题，最后到许多人共有的信念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a light that can go out and come back on.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏会熄灭也会重新亮起的灯。

branches.en: The first sense is the bare state of being awake.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是醒着这一基本状态。

branches.en: The second sense adds an object: something is noticed.
branches.cn: 第二个义项加上了对象：某件事被注意到。

branches.en: The third sense spreads that noticing across a whole group.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把这种注意扩展到整个群体。

branches.en: Being awake is the ground on which any noticing stands.
branches.cn: 醒着，是任何察觉得以成立的地面。

branches.en: One person's noticing becomes a group's consciousness when others agree.
branches.cn: 一个人的察觉，在别人认同后就成了群体的意识。

intro.en: Consciousness is conscious plus -ness, from Latin com-, with, and scire, to know.
intro.cn: consciousness 是 conscious 加 -ness，源自拉丁语 com-（与）与 scire（知道）。

latinIntro.en: The Latin know base sci- also appears in science, conscience and omniscient.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的知道词基 sci- 也出现在 science、conscience 与 omniscient 中。

items.exampleCN: 他在黎明时恢复了知觉。

items.example: She was conscious of the risk.
He consciously kept his voice low.
The image stayed in her subconscious.
items.exampleCN: 那个画面留在她的潜意识里。

items.meaning: the inner sense of right and wrong

items.exampleCN: 那个声音听起来无所不知。

definition_en: to agree to something, or official permission for something to happen
core_image: 合同末尾，笔尖在签名栏上停了一秒才落下
scene: 医生把手术同意书推到家属面前，等他们点头。Her parents consented to the trip.
sceneCN: 这里 consent 指「同意」（第 1 个义项：表示许可）；句意是她的父母同意了这趟旅行。

senses.title: Say yes
senses.definition: to agree to something or give permission for it
senses.definitionCN: 同意某事或给予许可
senses.example: She consented to the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 她同意接受采访。
senses.why: Two wills meet, and one of them stops resisting.
senses.whyCN: 两种意愿相遇，其中一种不再抵抗。

senses.title: Official permission
senses.definition: official agreement that allows something to happen
senses.definitionCN: 允许某事发生的正式同意
senses.example: The builder needs written consent from the owner.
senses.exampleCN: 施工方需要业主的书面同意。
senses.why: A spoken yes fades, so the law asks it to leave a mark.
senses.whyCN: 口头答应会消散，所以法律要求它留下痕迹。

senses.title: A shared view
senses.definition: general agreement among a group, an older and rarer sense
senses.definitionCN: 一群人的普遍一致，是较古老且少用的义项
senses.example: By common consent the plan was dropped.
senses.exampleCN: 经大家一致同意，这个计划被放弃了。
senses.why: When many feelings move the same way, no vote is needed.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人的感受朝同一方向走，就不需要投票了。

intro.en: Consent comes from Latin consentire, to feel together, from com-, together, and sentire, to feel.
intro.cn: consent 来自拉丁语 consentire，意为一起感受，由 com-（一起）与 sentire（感觉）构成。

items.en: Sentire meant to feel, perceive or think.
items.cn: sentire 意为感觉、察觉或思考。

items.en: Consentire meant to feel the same way as another.
items.cn: consentire 意为与另一个人感受相同。

items.en: The noun consensus named that shared feeling.
items.cn: 名词 consensus 指这种共同的感受。

items.en: Old French consentir carried the sense of agreeing.
items.cn: 古法语 consentir 带有同意的含义。

items.en: English consent first meant to agree or be of one mind.
items.cn: 英语 consent 最初指同意或心意一致。

items.en: It now also names formal permission in law and medicine.
items.cn: 如今它也指法律与医疗中的正式许可。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sound of consent, and the meaning group names other ways of saying yes.
note.cn: 形近组与 consent 读音相近，近义组列出其他表示答应的说法。

entries.definition: an opinion shared by most people
formal agreement to a plan
to feel angry about something unfair
to have the same opinion
to officially accept something
the right to do something given by someone

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from two people feeling the same way, then move to a signature and to a room that agrees without voting.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从两个人感受相同开始，再到一个签名，最后到不用投票就一致的房间。

normal.en: Con- is together and sent- is feel, so consent is to feel along with someone.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，sent- 是感觉，consent 就是跟着对方一起感受。

normal.en: A nod is the shortest contract in the world.
normal.cn: 一个点头，是世界上最简短的合同。

normal.en: Consent given in writing is a yes you cannot take back easily.
normal.cn: 写下来的同意，是难以轻易收回的答应。

normal.en: No consent, no entry: the same rule for doors and for bodies.
normal.cn: 没有同意就不许进：门如此，人也是如此。

normal.en: When everyone consents, the meeting ends early.
normal.cn: 大家都同意时，会就提前散了。

abstract.en: Picture a pen hovering above a line.
abstract.cn: 想象一支笔在一条横线上方悬着。

abstract.en: Picture two heads nodding at the same second.
abstract.cn: 想象两个头在同一秒点下去。

abstract.en: Picture a door opened from the inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门从里面被打开。

examples.en: He consented to the search of his bag.
examples.cn: 他同意接受检查他的包。

examples.en: No one may enter the site without consent.
examples.cn: 未经许可，任何人不得进入场地。

examples.en: Her consent was given in writing.
examples.cn: 她的同意是以书面形式给出的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 consent 记成 con（一起）加 sent（感觉）：两个人感觉到一起去了，自然就点头同意。

root: 源自拉丁语 consentire（com 一起 + sentire 感觉），本义是感受相同，后指同意、赞同与正式许可。

sensesIntro.en: From two feelings moving as one, to a signed permission, and finally to a whole group thinking alike.
sensesIntro.cn: 从两种感受合而为一，到签下的许可，最后到整个群体想法一致。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two heads nodding at the very same moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个头在同一瞬间点下去。

branches.en: The verb is the act of agreeing or allowing.
branches.cn: 动词义项就是同意或允许的动作。

branches.en: The noun sense is the permission that remains on record.
branches.cn: 名词义项是留在记录里的那份许可。

branches.en: The older sense is a group feeling the same way.
branches.cn: 较古老的义项是一群人感受相同。

branches.en: Saying yes and the paper that proves it are one process.
branches.cn: 说出同意与证明它的那张纸，是同一个过程。

branches.en: Both rest on people finding that their feelings match.
branches.cn: 两者都建立在人们发现彼此感受相合之上。

intro.en: Consent is built on Latin com-, together, plus sentire, to feel.
intro.cn: consent 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 sentire（感觉）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin feel base sent- also appears in assent, dissent, resent and sensation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的感觉词基 sent- 也出现在 assent、dissent、resent 与 sensation 中。

items.meaning: to feel the same and agree

items.exampleCN: 这是一个双方同意的决定。
两位法官写下了反对意见。

items.meaning: to feel anger again and again
items.exampleCN: 她对那条不公平的规定感到愤恨。

items.example: A cold sensation spread down his arm.
items.exampleCN: 一阵冰凉的感觉顺着手臂蔓延。

definition_en: a result of an action, or importance in a situation
core_image: 推倒第一张骨牌，后面的牌一张张跟着倒
scene: 他没带伞就出门，回来时浑身湿透。Skipping breakfast had clear consequences for his day.
sceneCN: 这里 consequence 指「后果」（第 1 个义项：行为带来的结果）；句意是不吃早饭对他这一天造成了明显的后果。

derivatives.zh: 随之发生的；作为结果的

senses.title: A result
senses.definition: a result that follows from an action or condition
senses.definitionCN: 由行为或情况引发的直接结果
senses.example: The consequence of the delay was a lost contract.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误的后果是丢了一份合同。
senses.why: Every action sets a line in motion, and the line arrives somewhere.
senses.whyCN: 每个行动都让一条线开始运动，而这条线终会抵达某处。

senses.title: Importance
senses.definition: importance or significance, often in the phrase of consequence
senses.definitionCN: 重要性或意义，常见于 of consequence 的说法
senses.example: The decision was of great consequence.
senses.exampleCN: 这个决定关系重大。
senses.why: Something that pulls many other things behind it must be heavy.
senses.whyCN: 能拉动许多别的东西的事物，本身一定很重。

senses.title: A logical conclusion
senses.definition: a conclusion drawn from a set of facts
senses.definitionCN: 由一组事实推出的结论
senses.example: From these facts one consequence is unavoidable.
senses.exampleCN: 由这些事实可以得出一个无法回避的结论。
senses.why: Reason walks forward, and this is the place it must stop.
senses.whyCN: 推理一路向前走，而这里就是它必须停下的地方。

intro.en: Consequence comes from Latin consequentia, a following after, from com-, together, and sequi, to follow.
intro.cn: consequence 来自拉丁语 consequentia，意为随后而来，由 com-（一起）与 sequi（跟随）构成。

items.en: Sequi meant to follow behind someone.
items.cn: sequi 意为跟在某人后面。

items.en: Consequi meant to follow after and reach the same point.
items.cn: consequi 意为随后跟到同一点。

items.en: Consequentia named what follows from something else.
items.cn: consequentia 指由别的事物引出的东西。

items.en: Old French consequence used the word for a result.
items.cn: 古法语 consequence 用这个词指结果。

items.en: English consequence first meant what follows in logic.
items.cn: 英语 consequence 最初指逻辑上随之而来的东西。

items.en: It now also means weight or importance.
items.cn: 如今它也指分量或重要性。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin follow base, and the meaning group names other results.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语跟随词基，近义组列出其他表示结果的词。

entries.definition: a set of things in a fixed order
entries.definitionCN: 按固定顺序排列的一系列事物

entries.definition: following as a result
as a result
what happens because of something else
the final effect of a process
a change caused by an action

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from falling dominoes, then move to the weight of a big decision and to a conclusion you cannot avoid.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从倒下的骨牌开始，再到重大决定的分量，最后到无法回避的结论。

normal.en: Con- is together and sequ- is follow, so a consequence is what follows an act.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，sequ- 是跟随，consequence 就是跟着行为而来的东西。

normal.en: One push on the first domino, and the whole row falls.
normal.cn: 推一下第一张骨牌，整排都会倒下。

normal.en: If you cannot carry the result, do not start the act.
normal.cn: 若你背不起结果，就别开始这个行为。

normal.en: Of little consequence means the thing weighs almost nothing.
normal.cn: of little consequence 意思是这件事几乎没有分量。

normal.en: A sequence is an order; a consequence is the price of that order.
normal.cn: sequence 是顺序，consequence 是这顺序要付的代价。

abstract.en: Picture a line of tiles tipping one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象一排骨牌一个接一个倒下。

abstract.en: Picture a stone dropped into still water.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗石子落进平静的水面。

abstract.en: Picture a hand paying a bill it forgot it made.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手去付一笔它忘了自己欠下的账。

examples.en: The consequence of the delay was a lost contract.
examples.cn: 这次延误的后果是丢掉了一份合同。

examples.en: He accepted the consequences of his choice.
examples.cn: 他接受了自己选择的后果。

examples.en: The decision was of great consequence to the town.
examples.cn: 这个决定对这座城镇关系重大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 consequence 记成 con（一起）加 sequ（跟随）加 ence：紧跟着行为一起到来的那件事，就是后果。

root: 源自拉丁语 consequentia（com 一起 + sequi 跟随），本义是随后而来之物，后指后果、推论与重要性。

sensesIntro.en: From what follows an act, to the weight that makes it matter, and finally to a conclusion forced by facts.
sensesIntro.cn: 从随行为而来的东西，到让它有分量的重要性，最后到事实逼出的结论。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one push, and the whole row of dominoes falls.
core.cn: 核心意象：推一下，整排骨牌倒下。

branches.en: The core sense is the result that follows an action.
branches.cn: 核心义项是随行为而来的结果。

branches.en: A result with many followers feels important.
branches.cn: 牵动许多后续的结果，就显得重要。

branches.en: In reasoning, the result is a conclusion.
branches.cn: 在推理中，这种结果就是结论。

branches.en: Serious consequences are just results heavy enough to notice.
branches.cn: 严重后果不过是重到让人不得不注意的结果。

branches.en: Both senses deal with weight, one of events and one of logic.
branches.cn: 两个义项都涉及分量，一个在事件上，一个在逻辑上。

intro.en: Consequence is built on Latin com-, together, plus sequi, to follow.
intro.cn: consequence 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 sequi（跟随）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin follow base sequ- also appears in sequence, sequel and consecutive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的跟随词基 sequ- 也出现在 sequence、sequel 与 consecutive 中。

items.exampleCN: 随之而来的延误并不长。

items.example: It rained and consequently we stayed.
items.exampleCN: 下雨了，因此我们留了下来。
这是一个影响重大的决定。

items.meaningCN: 按固定顺序排列的事物

items.meaning: to follow in order to catch

items.example: It rained for three consecutive days.

definition_en: to think about something carefully, or to regard it in a certain way
core_image: 桌上摊着两份合同，手指在纸边来回摩挲
scene: 她盯着两份合同，笔尖在纸上轻轻点了两下。She needed a week to consider the offer.
sceneCN: 这里 consider 指「考虑」（第 1 个义项：在决定前仔细思考）；句意是她需要一周时间来考虑这个提议。

senses.title: Think about
senses.definition: to think about something before deciding
senses.definitionCN: 在做出决定之前仔细思考某事
senses.example: We are considering moving to another city.
senses.exampleCN: 我们正在考虑搬到另一座城市。
senses.why: A choice is weighed in the mind before it is made by the hand.
senses.whyCN: 选择先在心里过秤，然后才由手做出。

senses.title: Regard as
senses.definition: to have an opinion about someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某事物持有某种看法
senses.example: Many consider him the best player alive.
senses.exampleCN: 很多人认为他是当今最好的球员。
senses.why: The mind takes a position and then stands there.
senses.whyCN: 头脑选定一个位置，然后就站在那里。

senses.title: Take into account
senses.definition: to take someone's feelings or needs into account
senses.definitionCN: 把某人的感受或需要纳入考虑
senses.example: She never considers how others feel.
senses.exampleCN: 她从不考虑别人的感受。
senses.why: Thinking well means letting another person into the room.
senses.whyCN: 好好思考，意味着让别人也走进这间屋子。

intro.en: Consider comes from Latin considerare, to examine closely, probably from com-, together, and sidus, star, as if reading the sky.
intro.cn: consider 来自拉丁语 considerare，意为仔细审视，可能由 com-（一起）与 sidus（星）构成，仿佛在观测星空。

items.en: Sidus meant a star or a group of stars.
items.cn: sidus 意为星辰或一组星。

items.en: Considerare may have meant to observe the stars carefully.
items.cn: considerare 可能原指仔细观测星象。

items.en: From watching the sky it came to mean examining anything.
items.cn: 从仰望天空，它转而表示审视任何事物。

items.en: Old French considerer kept the sense of thinking over.
items.cn: 古法语 considerer 保留了反复思量的含义。

items.en: English consider first meant to look at something with care.
items.cn: 英语 consider 最初指带着用心去看。

items.en: It now covers thinking, judging and taking others into account.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖思考、判断与顾及他人。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on the consider family, and the meaning group names other ways of thinking something over.
note.cn: 形近组是 consider 家族，近义组列出其他表示反复思量的词。

entries.definition: large enough to be noticed
careful about other people's feelings
careful thought about something
to think about something for a long time
to think carefully before deciding
to look at or think of in a certain way

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from reading the stars, then move to two papers on a desk and to a friend you finally remember to ask.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从观测星辰开始，再到桌上摊着的两份文件，最后到终于想起来去问的那位朋友。

normal.en: Con- is together and sider- is star, so consider is to line up the stars before acting.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，sider- 是星，consider 就是行动前先把星象排一排。

normal.en: Two papers on a desk: the mind walks between them.
normal.cn: 桌上两份文件，心思在两者之间来回走。

normal.en: All things considered means the scales were fully loaded first.
normal.cn: all things considered 意思是天平上先放满了东西。

normal.en: To consider others is to give them a chair at your table.
normal.cn: consider 别人，就是给他们在你桌边留一把椅子。

normal.en: A good decision is a slow decision that looks like a fast one.
normal.cn: 好决定是慢的，只是看起来很快。

abstract.en: Picture a hand turning a coin over twice.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把一枚硬币翻来覆去。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp above two papers late at night.
abstract.cn: 想象深夜一盏灯照着两份文件。

abstract.en: Picture a pause before a signature.
abstract.cn: 想象签名之前的一段停顿。

examples.en: We are considering moving to another city.
examples.cn: 我们正在考虑搬到另一座城市。

examples.en: Many consider her the best teacher here.
examples.cn: 很多人认为她是这里最好的老师。

examples.en: He never considers how his words sound.
examples.cn: 他从不考虑自己的话听起来是什么滋味。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 consider 记成 con（一起）加 sider（星）：古人行动前先一起看星象，引申为把各种可能都想一遍，即考虑。

root: 源自拉丁语 considerare（com 一起 + sidus 星辰），本义可能是观测星象，后指仔细审视、思考与顾及。

sensesIntro.en: From scanning the sky, to weighing options, to forming an opinion, and at last to remembering other people.
sensesIntro.cn: 从扫视天空，到权衡选项，再到形成看法，最后到把别人放在心上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: eyes lifted to the stars, then lowered to a choice.
core.cn: 核心意象：眼睛先抬向星辰，再落到一个选择上。

branches.en: The first sense is thinking before deciding.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是决定之前的思考。

branches.en: The second sense is the opinion that such thought produces.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是这种思考所得出的看法。

branches.en: The third sense turns thought toward other people.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把思虑转向他人。

branches.en: Weighing facts and judging them are two steps of one act.
branches.cn: 权衡事实与给出判断，是同一个动作的两步。

branches.en: A person who counts others as real is considered kind.
branches.cn: 把别人当回事的人，会被认为善良。

intro.en: Consider is built on Latin considerare, possibly from com-, together, and sidus, star.
intro.cn: consider 由拉丁语 considerare 构成，可能源自 com-（一起）与 sidus（星辰）。

latinIntro.en: The star base sider- also appears in sidereal, and the related desire came from desiderare, to long for the stars.
latinIntro.cn: 星辰词基 sider- 也出现在 sidereal 中，而相关的 desire 来自 desiderare，意为向往星辰。

items.example: Consider the price before you buy.

items.exampleCN: 这个计划正在考虑之中。
她想旅行的愿望越来越强。

items.example: A sidereal day is slightly shorter.

definition_zh: 相当大的；相当多的；值得考虑的
definition_en: large enough in amount or degree to be noticed and counted
core_image: 账单上的数字比预想多出一大截
scene: 他打开账单，发现数字比预想多出一大截。The repair cost a considerable sum.
sceneCN: 这里 considerable 指「相当大的」（第 1 个义项：数量或程度大到值得注意）；句意是这次维修花了一笔相当可观的钱。

pos.zh: 相当大的；相当多的；值得考虑的

derivatives.zh: 相当大地；在很大程度上

senses.title: Large in amount
senses.definition: large enough in amount or degree to be noticed
senses.definitionCN: 数量或程度大到值得注意
senses.example: The repair cost a considerable sum.
senses.exampleCN: 这次维修花了一笔相当可观的钱。
senses.why: A size that makes you stop and look is a size that counts.
senses.whyCN: 大到让你停下来看的规模，就是有分量的规模。

senses.title: Worth attention
senses.definition: important enough to deserve attention, an older and rarer sense
senses.definitionCN: 重要到值得关注，是较古老且少用的义项
senses.example: It was a considerable event in local history.
senses.exampleCN: 这是地方史上值得重视的事件。
senses.why: What deserves thought is what pulls the eye toward it.
senses.whyCN: 值得思考的东西，会把目光拉向自己。

intro.en: Considerable is consider plus -able, from Latin considerare, to examine, and it first meant able to be considered.
intro.cn: considerable 是 consider 加 -able，源自动词 considerare（审视），最初意为值得被考虑的。

items.en: Considerare meant to examine something closely.
items.cn: considerare 意为仔细审视某物。

items.en: The suffix -abilis marked what could be done.
items.cn: 词尾 -abilis 表示可以被怎样对待。

items.en: French considerable meant worthy of attention.
items.cn: 法语 considerable 意为值得注意的。

items.en: English considerable first meant able to be considered.
items.cn: 英语 considerable 最初指可以被考虑的。

items.en: It shifted to mean great in size or amount.
items.cn: 它的含义转向规模或数量很大。

items.en: Today the size sense is the everyday one.
items.cn: 今天日常使用的主要是表示规模大的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group is the consider family, and the meaning group names other words for a large amount.
note.cn: 形近组是 consider 家族，近义组列出其他表示数量大的词。

large in size, value or importance

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a bill larger than expected, then move to progress you can measure and to an event people still discuss.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从比预想更大的账单开始，再到可以量出的进步，最后到人们仍在谈论的事件。

normal.en: Considerable means big enough that you must consider it.
normal.cn: considerable 就是大到你必须把它考虑进去。

normal.en: A considerable sum is one that changes the plan.
normal.cn: 一笔可观的款子，是能改变计划的那种钱。

normal.en: Considerable progress can be measured, not merely felt.
normal.cn: 相当大的进步是量得出来的，不只是感觉。

normal.en: If nobody would notice its absence, it is not considerable.
normal.cn: 若它不在了也没人察觉，那它就称不上相当大。

normal.en: Think of a shadow long enough to reach the wall.
normal.cn: 想想一道长到能碰到墙的影子。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of coins higher than the cup.
abstract.cn: 想象一摞比杯子还高的硬币。

abstract.en: Picture a gap in the road you cannot step over.
abstract.cn: 想象路上一道你迈不过去的缺口。

abstract.en: Picture a number that makes a hand pause.
abstract.cn: 想象一个让手停下来的数字。

examples.en: The repair cost a considerable sum.
examples.cn: 这次维修花了一笔相当可观的钱。

examples.en: She spent considerable time on the report.
examples.cn: 她在这份报告上花了相当多的时间。

examples.en: The project made considerable progress this year.

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 considerable 记成 consider（考虑）加 able（能）：大到必须被考虑进来的程度，就是相当大的。

root: 由拉丁语 considerare（审视）加 -able 构成，原意是值得被考虑的，后转为数量或程度相当大的。

sensesIntro.en: From something worth thinking about, to a size big enough that it forces itself into your thinking.

branches.en: The main sense is size large enough to be counted.

branches.en: The older sense is importance that earns attention.

branches.en: A large amount of anything becomes important by its weight.
branches.cn: 任何东西的数量一大，就凭分量变得重要。

branches.en: Comparatives like more considerable are rare but regular.

branches.en: In old texts the word can mean worthy of respect.

latinIntro.en: The star base sider- also appears in sidereal and in the history of desire.
latinIntro.cn: 星辰词基 sider- 也出现在 sidereal 以及 desire 的历史中。

items.exampleCN: 经过长时间考虑，她同意了。

definition_zh: 相当大地；在很大程度上
definition_en: by a large amount or degree
core_image: 水位一夜之间涨到台阶的第三级
scene: 一夜大雨之后，河里的水位明显升高。The road became considerably more dangerous after dark.
sceneCN: 这里 considerably 指「相当大地」（第 1 个义项：程度很大地）；句意是天黑之后这条路变得危险多了。

pos.zh: 相当大地；在很大程度上

senses.title: To a large degree
senses.definition: by a large amount or degree
senses.definitionCN: 在数量或程度上很大地
senses.example: The cost rose considerably last year.

senses.why: The change is too big to be waved away as small.

senses.title: Before comparatives
senses.definition: used with more or a comparative to mean much
senses.definitionCN: 与 more 或比较级连用，表示…得多

senses.exampleCN: 新发动机安静得多。
senses.why: A comparison needs a weight word to show the gap is wide.

senses.title: In a notable way
senses.definition: in a way that is easy to notice
senses.definitionCN: 以容易被人察觉的方式
senses.example: Her accent changed considerably over the year.
senses.exampleCN: 这一年里她的口音变化很明显。
senses.why: Some changes announce themselves before you measure them.
senses.whyCN: 有些变化在你测量之前就先自己报了名。

intro.en: Considerably is considerable plus -ly, from Latin considerare, to examine closely.
intro.cn: considerably 是 considerable 加 -ly，源头是拉丁语 considerare，意为仔细审视。

items.en: Considerare meant to look at something with care.
items.cn: considerare 意为带着留心去看某物。

items.en: The adjective considerabilis meant worth noticing.
items.cn: 形容词 considerabilis 意为值得注意的。

items.en: English considerable first meant able to be considered.
items.cn: 英语 considerable 最初指可以被考虑的。

items.en: The sense shifted toward large in size or amount.
items.cn: 它的含义转向规模或数量很大。

items.en: The adverb considerably grew common with comparatives.
items.cn: 副词 considerably 开始常与比较级连用。

items.en: It now simply strengthens how large a change is.
items.cn: 如今它只是加强说明变化有多大。

note.en: The look-alike group is the consider family, and the meaning group names other adverbs of large degree.

careful thought about something

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a river that climbed the steps, then move to a quieter engine and to an accent that changed.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从涨上台阶的河水开始，再到更安静的发动机，最后到变了样的口音。

normal.en: Considerably is considerable turned into an adverb: in a big way.
normal.cn: considerably 是 considerable 的副词，意思是以很大的方式。

normal.en: It almost always leans on a comparative: more, better, higher.
normal.cn: 它几乎总靠在比较级上：more、better、higher。

normal.en: A considerably higher price is one you feel before you calculate.
normal.cn: 高出不少的价格，你在算之前就先感觉到了。

normal.en: If the change needs a photo to prove it, it is considerable.
normal.cn: 若这变化需要照片才能证明，那就算相当大了。

normal.en: One word adds weight to the scale of any sentence.
normal.cn: 一个词，就能给任何句子的天平加砝码。

abstract.en: Picture water touching the third step of a stair.
abstract.cn: 想象水漫到楼梯的第三级。

abstract.en: Picture two lines on a graph pulling far apart.
abstract.cn: 想象图上两条线越拉越开。

abstract.en: Picture a needle moving well past the middle mark.
abstract.cn: 想象指针远远越过中间那条刻度。

examples.en: The road became considerably more dangerous after dark.
examples.cn: 天黑之后这条路变得危险多了。

examples.en: Prices have risen considerably this year.
examples.cn: 今年物价大幅上涨。

examples.en: Her writing improved considerably after the course.
examples.cn: 上完这门课之后，她的写作进步很大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 considerably 记成 considerable（相当大的）加 ly：用相当大的幅度去做某件事，就是相当大地。

root: 由拉丁语 considerare（审视）经 considerable 加 -ly 构成，表示程度或数量上很大的方式。

sensesIntro.en: From a plain large degree, to its usual place before comparatives, and finally to a change anyone can see.
sensesIntro.cn: 从单纯表示程度大，到常站在比较级前面，最后到人人都看得见的变化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle pushed well past the middle mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：指针被推过中间刻度很远。

branches.en: The main sense is a large degree of change.
branches.cn: 主要义项是变化程度很大。

branches.en: Before a comparative it marks a wide gap.
branches.cn: 放在比较级前面时，它标出很大的差距。

branches.en: The third sense stresses that the change is visible.
branches.cn: 第三个义项强调这种变化看得见。

branches.en: The adverb either stands alone or leans on a comparison.
branches.cn: 这个副词要么单独站着，要么靠在比较上。

branches.en: A gap wide enough to see is a gap worth the word.
branches.cn: 宽到看得见的差距，才配得上这个词。

intro.en: Considerably is considerable plus -ly, from Latin considerare, to examine.
intro.cn: considerably 是 considerable 加 -ly，源自拉丁语 considerare（审视）。

latinIntro.cn: 星辰词基 sider- 也出现在 sidereal 中，desire 也共享同一个古老词根。

items.exampleCN: 随后出现了相当长的延误。
把两个答案都考虑一下。

items.example: Sidereal time drifts from clock time.
items.exampleCN: 恒星时与钟表时间会错开。

definition_zh: 考虑；需要考虑的因素；体谅
definition_en: the act of thinking carefully about something, or a fact that must be weighed
core_image: 桌上摊着几张纸，一个人托着下巴逐条权衡
scene: 面试前夜，她把每个条件在纸上排了一遍。After long consideration, she accepted the offer.
sceneCN: 这里 consideration 指「仔细考虑」（第 1 个义项：对某事反复权衡）；句意是经过长时间的考虑，她接受了这份工作。

pos.zh: 考虑；需要考虑的因素；体谅

senses.title: Careful thought
senses.definition: the act of thinking about something carefully before acting
senses.definitionCN: 行动之前对某事反复思考
senses.example: After much consideration, they chose the cheaper plan.
senses.exampleCN: 经过再三考虑，他们选择了更便宜的那个方案。
senses.why: A decision made in a hurry often misses what a slow look would catch.
senses.whyCN: 匆忙作出的决定，常常漏掉慢看时能看见的东西。

senses.title: A fact to weigh
senses.definition: something that must be taken into account when deciding
senses.definitionCN: 做决定时必须纳入权衡的事情
senses.example: Cost is only one consideration here.
senses.exampleCN: 在这里，成本只是需要考虑的一个因素。
senses.why: A good choice needs more than one item on the scale.
senses.whyCN: 好的选择需要天平上不只放一样东西。

senses.title: Thought for others
senses.definition: kind attention to the feelings of other people
senses.definitionCN: 对他人感受的体贴照顾
senses.example: He showed no consideration for the tired staff.
senses.exampleCN: 他对疲惫的员工毫不体谅。
senses.why: The same mind that weighs facts can also weigh feelings.
senses.whyCN: 权衡事实的那颗心，也能权衡别人的感受。

intro.en: Consideration comes from Latin considerare, to look at closely, a word once linked to sidus, a star, as if reading the sky.
intro.cn: consideration 来自拉丁语 considerare，意为仔细察看，旧说与 sidus（星星）有关，仿佛观星以定吉凶。

items.en: Sidus meant star, and considerare may once have meant to observe the stars.
items.cn: sidus 意为星星，considerare 最初可能指观察星象。

items.en: Considerare widened to mean examining anything with care.
items.cn: considerare 的词义扩大为仔细察看任何事物。

items.en: The noun consideratio named the act of careful looking.
items.cn: 名词 consideratio 指仔细察看这一行为。

items.en: French consideration carried the sense of respectful regard.
items.cn: 法语 consideration 带有尊重与顾念的含义。

items.en: English consideration first meant careful thought before a choice.
items.cn: 英语 consideration 最初指做选择前的仔细思考。

items.en: It now also names a single fact that must be weighed.
items.cn: 如今它也指必须纳入权衡的某一因素。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words from the same consider- family, and the meaning group names other kinds of careful thought.
note.cn: 形近组收的是同一个 consider- 词族的词，近义组列出其他表示仔细思量的说法。

entries.definition: thinking about the feelings of other people
large enough to be important
used to say that something is true when you think of the facts
the activity of thinking, or an idea produced by it
long and careful discussion before a decision
attention or care given to someone

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a slow look at the facts, then move to the single fact that tips a choice and to care for other people.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从慢慢端详事实开始，再到压动选择的那一个因素，最后落到对他人的体谅。

normal.en: Con- is together and sider is star, so consideration is reading the sky before you move.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，sider 是星星，consideration 就是先看星象再行动。

normal.en: A table with three papers on it: that is consideration at work.
normal.cn: 桌上摊着三张纸，这就是考虑正在进行的样子。

normal.en: One factor is not a decision, so consideration puts several on the scale.
normal.cn: 一个因素不成决定，所以考虑要把好几样放上天平。

normal.en: Consideration for others is the same word turned toward feelings.
normal.cn: 体谅不过是同一个词转向了感受这一边。

normal.en: Look twice, then act once.
normal.cn: 看两遍，再动手一次。

abstract.en: Picture a hand holding a scale that is still moving.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手扶着一架仍在晃动的天平。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp over a page full of small notes.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯照着一页密密麻麻的小字。

abstract.en: Picture a chair pulled out for someone who looks tired.
abstract.cn: 想象有人为一位显出疲态的人拉开椅子。

examples.en: After much consideration, she turned down the offer.
examples.cn: 经过反复考虑，她拒绝了那份邀约。

examples.en: Safety must be the first consideration in this design.
examples.cn: 在这个设计里，安全必须是首要的考虑。

examples.en: He treats his staff with real consideration.
examples.cn: 他对员工十分体谅。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 consideration 记成 con（一起）加 sider（星星）加 ation：像古人一起看星推演吉凶那样反复权衡，就是考虑。

root: 源自拉丁语 considerare（仔细察看），旧说与 sidus（星星）有关，仿佛观星以定吉凶，后指考虑、需要权衡的因素与体谅。

sensesIntro.en: From slow looking, to the facts that demand a look, and finally to looking after other people.
sensesIntro.cn: 从慢慢察看，到必须察看的事实，最后到照看别人的感受。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale on a table with papers on both sides.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上放着一架天平，两边都压着纸。

branches.en: Careful thought slows the hand before it moves.
branches.cn: 仔细考虑让手在行动之前先慢下来。

branches.en: A single consideration can change the whole balance.
branches.cn: 一个因素就能改变整个平衡。

branches.en: The same habit of mind turns into kindness toward people.
branches.cn: 同一种思维习惯转向人，就成了体贴。

branches.en: Both senses put something on a scale and wait for it to settle.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是把东西放上天平，等它稳定下来。

branches.en: A person can be the factor that a careful mind weighs.
branches.cn: 人本身也可以成为那颗细心的心所权衡的因素。

intro.en: Consideration is built on Latin con-, together, plus considerare, to examine.
intro.cn: consideration 由拉丁语 con-（一起）与 considerare（察看）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin star base sider- also appears in sidereal, while the consider- family runs through consider and considerable.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的星词基 sider- 也出现在 sidereal 中，而 consider- 词族贯穿 consider 与 considerable。

items.meaning: the act of weighing something in the mind
items.meaningCN: 在心里权衡某事的行为
items.exampleCN: 这个计划正在考虑之中。

items.meaning: to examine something in the mind
worth noticing because of its size
